title: Metering
description: config/metering.yaml: the Treasury's settings (PRD 14.1, 14.4, 17.3; FR-MTR-02, -03, -04, -08). What the PRD states as a rule is const: the 15% reserve, the budget request at 80% and the reconciliation tolerance of 10%. Caps and daily spend limits are config with the PRD demo defaults. The credit unit (US$0.005) stays in config/prices.yaml. Rules a schema cannot express are MT-01.. in contracts/metering.rules.md.

treasury.description: Reserve, then commit (PRD 14.1). Each step reserves its estimate times (1 + reserve_margin) before running and commits the actual cost after; a step that cannot reserve waits (FR-MTR-02). At request_at of the approved budget the Director raises budget.requested (FR-MTR-03). Both are fixed by the PRD; minimum and maximum repeat each const so generated Python checks it too.

caps.description: Credit caps per run, per user per day and per org per day, all from config (PRD 14.1). Demo defaults: 300 credits per public run (17.3); 1,500 credits per pilot tester per day (17.3); no separate org cap (BQ-42). null means no cap at that scope, and every key is still required so that no scope is left out by accident. A day is the UTC calendar day (BQ-44).

cap.description: Credits above zero, or null for no cap at that scope.

spend.description: US dollars of model spend per day for the deployment (PRD 14.1, 17.3; demo defaults US$15 soft, US$25 hard on tilo-demo). The soft cap raises an alert; the hard cap flips the kill switch, so the public link turns replay-only (NFR-24, FR-MTR-04). daily_usd_hard is at least daily_usd_soft (MT-01).

reconciliation.description: Daily reconciliation (PRD 14.4, FR-MTR-08): ledger credits times US$0.005 must match billed model spend within the tolerance, fixed at 10% by the PRD; larger drift raises an alert and freezes new claims in the deck until explained (MT-02). billing_services names the billing-export services counted as model spend; empty until one is named.

billing_service.description: A service name as the billing export writes it: letters, digits, spaces and . _ ( ) -, starting with a letter or digit.
